notes.claim: For a gear train the gear ratio is the input speed divided by the output speed; for two gears it matches the teeth or radius ratio.
A belt that does not slip moves at the same speed as the edge of both pulleys.
When a gearbox reduces speed it raises torque in proportion, and a real gearbox loses some power to friction so output power is smaller than input.
Marine diesel engines commonly use a reduction gearbox so the propeller shaft turns slower than the engine.
Shaft misalignment causes vibration, noise and premature bearing, coupling or shaft failure.
Shaft misalignment has no measurable effect on motor efficiency; its harm is vibration, heat and wear (for i7).

sources.quote: It follows that if the speed is reduced, the torque is increased and vice versa. In a real gear box. power is lost through friction and the power output is smaller than the power input.

sources.quote: Most marine diesel engines have a reduction gearbox, which makes the shaft turn slower than the engine, at a speed more suitable for the propeller.

sources.title: The Importance of Motor Shaft Alignment — US Department of Energy
sources.quote: Misalignment produces excessive vibration, noise, coupling, and bearing temperature increases, and premature bearing, coupling, or shaft failure.

sources.title: The Importance of Motor Shaft Alignment — US Department of Energy
sources.quote: While misalignment has no measurable effect on motor efficiency, correct shaft alignment ensures the smooth, efficient transmission of power from the motor to the driven equipment.
